meta.title: The Lantern of Hollowmere
meta.blurb: A drowned village, a ferrywoman who will not talk, and a bell that still rings under the water every night at the same hour. You came to find out why.
meta.author: ZeroRoll example story

world: Hollowmere was a lake village until the dam upriver failed forty years ago. Now its roofs sit a few feet under black, still water, and the only way across is Odda's ferry, pulled hand over hand along an iron chain. Every night at the third hour a bell rings somewhere under the lake. Lanterns burn blue near it. The people who moved to the shore say the drowned are not resting, and they do not say it loudly.
tone: Quiet, eerie and tender. Dread that turns out to be grief. Small kindnesses matter.
playerRole: A travelling lamplighter sent by the river guild to find out why boats keep turning back at Hollowmere. You carry a brass lantern, flint and steel, a coil of rope and a guild letter nobody here cares about.
narratorStyle: Close second person, present tense. Concrete sensory detail: cold water, wet rope, lamp smoke. Let silences sit. Dialogue is short and plain.

cast.name: Odda
cast.appearance: A broad woman in her sixties with cropped iron-grey hair, a weathered red face, pale blue eyes, a man's oilskin coat two sizes too big and rope-scarred hands.
cast.voice: Few words, flat and dry, sometimes a joke so deadpan it takes a moment to land.
cast.stance: Suspicious of guild folk. Warms slowly to anyone who works beside her without being asked.

cast.name: Maelis
cast.appearance: A girl of about fifteen made of lake water and blue light, long dark hair floating as if she is still underwater, a bell-ringer's grey smock, bare feet that never touch the floor.
cast.voice: Soft and echoing, as if heard through a wall. She repeats the last word others say when she is frightened.
cast.stance: Lonely and afraid of being forgotten. She rings the bell so someone will remember the village.

odda_trust.description: How far Odda trusts the player. She takes them across at 1 or more.

lantern_lit.description: The player's lantern is burning again after the crossing put it out.

knows_name.description: The player has learned the bell-ringer's name, Maelis.

spared_spirit.description: The player chose to free Maelis by remembering her rather than breaking the bell.

took_shard.description: The player broke the bell and took its blue glass shard.

beats.title: Odda's Landing
beats.sceneBrief: Dusk at the ferry landing. Odda is mending the ferry chain and refuses to take guild folk across: the last one laughed at the bell and fell in. She lost her younger sister Maelis in the flood, but will not say so yet. She will take the player across once they earn a little trust, by helping with the chain, by being honest about why they came, or by showing they take the bell seriously.

choices.label: Help Odda haul the heavy chain
choices.outcome:
You grab the other end of the chain and haul. It's heavy and freezing and stinks of the lake. Together, you get it back on the winch.

Odda looks at you sideways. Grunts. It might be thanks. "Most guild folk wouldn't dirty their hands," she says. Something in her face eases, a little.

choices.label: Tell her plainly why the guild sent you
choices.outcome:
You tell her plainly: the guild wants to know why the bell rings, and whether the lake is safe for boats. That's all. You're not here to laugh.

Odda studies your face for a long time. "Honest, at least," she says. "That's more than the last one." She doesn't say yes. But she doesn't say no either.

choices.label: Ask about the bell under the lake
choices.outcome:
You ask her about the bell under the lake.

Odda goes very still. "Rings at the third hour. Every night. Since the flood." She looks out at the tower. "My little sister used to ring it. Before." She stops, and won't say more. But you can see it costs her something to have said that much.

choices.label: Ask her to take you across now

beats.hint: Odda's chain slips and she curses at it, alone, clearly needing another pair of hands.
beats.page:
Dusk at the ferry landing on Hollowmere lake. The water is flat and grey and very still.

Out in the middle of the lake, the top of an old bell tower pokes up through the surface like a finger. Beneath it, they say, a whole village is drowned. And every night, at the third hour, a bell rings under the water.

The ferrywoman, Odda, is mending the ferry chain with cold red hands. She doesn't look up. "Guild, are you?" She spits into the reeds. "Last guild man I took across laughed at the bell. Fell in. Never came up."

She hauls at the chain. It slips. She curses at it, alone.

She won't take you across. Not yet. Not until she has some reason to trust you.

beats.title: The Crossing
beats.sceneBrief: Halfway across, a cold wind off the water snuffs the player's lantern. Below the ferry, blue lights drift between drowned rooftops and voices murmur a name. Odda will not row in the dark: they need the lantern burning to find the bell tower. If the player listens to the voices they can learn the name Maelis.

choices.label: Strike flint and relight the lantern
choices.outcome:
You strike your flint with numb fingers. Once. Twice. A spark. The wick catches, and the lantern blooms gold again.

Odda lets out a breath and picks up the oars. "Good," she says. "Now we can see where we're going."

choices.label: Lean over the side and listen to the voices
choices.outcome:
You lean over the side of the ferry, close to the black water, and listen.

The voices are soft, like people talking in another room. They're all saying the same name, over and over, gently, the way you'd call a child home for supper.

Maelis. Maelis. Maelis.

Behind you, Odda has gone very quiet.

choices.label: Tell Odda to keep pulling toward the tower

beats.hint: Odda mutters that she has rowed this lake blind before, and it nearly drowned her. She will not do it again without a light.
beats.page:
Odda rows. The ferry slides out across the black water, the lantern at the bow throwing a small circle of gold.

Halfway across, a cold wind comes off the lake, sudden as a slap, and snuffs your lantern out.

Darkness. Then, below the ferry, blue lights. They drift between the drowned rooftops down there, slow, like people walking home. And voices: soft, murmuring, all saying the same thing. A name.

Odda has stopped rowing. "I've rowed this lake blind before," she says. "It nearly drowned me. I'll not do it again without a light."

beats.title: The Bell Tower
beats.sceneBrief: The top of the old bell tower stands above the water like an island. Inside, stairs lead down into the flooded dark. A girl made of water and light, Maelis, watches the player from the stairwell but flees whenever she is called 'spirit' or 'ghost'. She will only come close to someone who knows her name. The parish board on the wall lists the bell-ringers; the last name is hers. The player may also give up and leave.

choices.label: Wipe the moss off the parish board
choices.outcome:
You wipe the moss off the old wooden board with your sleeve. It's the parish board: the names of the bell-ringers of Hollowmere, carved one under another, going back a hundred years.

The last name on the list is fresh-cut, the letters still sharp: MAELIS.

choices.label: Ask Odda who rang the bell before the flood
choices.outcome:
You ask Odda who rang the bell before the flood.

She doesn't answer for a long time. Then, very quietly: "My sister. Maelis. She was ringing it to warn everyone when the dam broke. She was still ringing it when the water came in." Odda's voice cracks. "She saved half the village. Not herself."

choices.label: Go down the stairs toward the bell
Get back in the ferry and leave

beats.hint: Odda's lantern light catches carved letters on a moss-covered board by the door.
beats.page:
The ferry bumps against the top of the bell tower, which stands above the water like a small stone island. Inside, a stair leads down, down, into the flooded dark.

And on the stair, watching you, is a girl made of water and light. She glows faintly blue. Her hair drifts as if she's still underwater.

When you call out to her, "Spirit! Ghost!", she flinches and flees down the stairs.

Odda's lantern light catches something on the wall by the door: carved letters on a moss-covered wooden board.

She won't come close to a stranger. Only to someone who knows who she is.

beats.title: The Drowned Bell
beats.sceneBrief: At the bottom of the stairs, in an air pocket under the tower, hangs the bell, its rope wrapped around Maelis's wrists. Its lip is set with a shard of blue lantern glass that keeps her bound here. Breaking the bell frees the glass, a valuable relic the guild would pay for, but scatters Maelis with it. Saying her name aloud and promising the village will be remembered lets her ring it one last time and rest. Odda, if she trusts the player, comes down too and recognises her sister.

choices.label: Say her name and promise Hollowmere will be remembered
Break the bell and take the blue shard
Ask Maelis why she keeps ringing
choices.outcome:
You ask Maelis why she keeps ringing the bell.

Her voice is like water over stones. "Because nobody came back. Nobody remembers. If I stop ringing, Hollowmere is gone. Really gone." She looks at the rope around her wrists. "Someone has to remember us."

beats.page:
At the bottom of the stairs, in a pocket of air beneath the tower, hangs the drowned bell.

Its rope is wrapped around the wrists of the girl made of water and light. Maelis. Set into the bell's lip is a shard of blue lantern glass, glowing, humming. It's what keeps her bound here, ringing, every night, forever.

The shard is a relic. The guild would pay a fortune for it. Breaking the bell would free it, and scatter Maelis like spray.

Or you could do something harder, and simpler. You could say her name.

Maelis looks at you, waiting.

beats.title: The Bell Rings Once
beats.sceneBrief: Maelis rings the bell one last time, a clear note that carries to the shore, and the blue lights go out one by one like people closing doors for the night. If Odda is there, the sisters say goodbye. The lake is just a lake again. The player rows back at dawn with something to write in the guild letter that is not a report.
beats.page:
"Maelis," you say. "Your name is Maelis. And Hollowmere will be remembered. I promise."

She smiles. For the first time, she smiles.

She rings the bell one last time, a clear, pure note that carries across the whole lake to the shore. And one by one, the blue lights go out beneath the water, like people closing their doors for the night.

If Odda came down with you, she's weeping, holding out her hands to her little sister, and Maelis touches them, just once, before she fades.

The lake is just a lake again. You row back at dawn, and in your guild letter, you write something that isn't a report.

beats.title: Keeper of the Shard
beats.sceneBrief: The bell cracks and the shard comes free, warm and humming. Maelis comes apart into a hundred small lights that drift away under the water. The bell will never ring again and the boats will cross safely. Odda rows back without a word. The guild pays well. Sometimes, at the third hour, the shard is cold.
beats.page:
You break the bell.

It cracks with a sound like a scream, and the shard comes free in your hand, warm and humming.

Maelis comes apart into a hundred small blue lights. They drift away under the water like sparks, and are gone.

The bell will never ring again. The boats will cross safely now.

Odda rows you back without a word. The guild pays you well, more money than you've ever seen.

Sometimes, at the third hour of the night, the shard in your pocket goes cold.

beats.title: The Long Way Home
beats.sceneBrief: The player leaves the tower and the lake behind. Odda takes them back in silence. That night, from the shore, the bell rings again at the third hour, and the player writes in the guild letter that Hollowmere cannot be crossed.
beats.page:
You climb back into the ferry. "Take me back," you say.

Odda rows you to the shore in silence. She doesn't seem surprised. Maybe she's glad.

That night, from your room at the inn, you hear it: at the third hour, the bell rings under the water, again, as it always has.

You sit by the window until dawn. Then you write your guild letter. Hollowmere, you write, cannot be crossed.
